input.brief: Parkan Group: regional electrical distributor (13 branches, 1700+ dealers), government infrastructure electrical contractor (hospitals, smart-city lighting, 4100+ streetlights), and new PARKAN wire & cable brand; audience dealers and investors

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Object on the seam
hero.blueprint: A white or very pale page organised by one change of tone. A square-cornered panel one step darker than the page (a flat pale blue-grey or warm grey) fills the top 44% of the viewport inside 12px margins; the page colour runs below it. The object, photographed on a plain background and blended with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, straddles the seam between the two tones: it is about 62% of the viewport wide, starts at column 6 and runs off the right edge, with its upper half over the panel and its lower half over the page. Type is small and exact. The headline is two lines at 24px in medium weight, far left on columns 1–3 at a 32px margin, its first baseline resting exactly on the seam; the second line is set in the softer ink. One supporting sentence at 15px, max 34ch, sits 120px lower on the same margin with the single action as a small rectangular button under it. A plain top row inside the panel at 14px: wordmark left, three text links centred, one text link right.
hero.mobile: The tonal panel takes the top 46svh. The object is 120vw wide, centred on the seam and cropped by the right edge. The headline sits just under the seam at 22px on two lines at a 20px margin, with the sentence at 15px beneath and then the button. The wordmark sits top-left inside the panel; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: Two short sentences at 24px, one per line and up to about 28 characters each, the second in the softer ink.

type.note: One neo-grotesk doing everything: semibold headings pulled tight, small regular text, no capitals and no second voice. Suits software, hardware and studio pages that want to look exact and unshowy.

photos.title: City by day
photos.treatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Figure on the photograph's edge
sections.blueprint: One full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 88svh, and one figure set on it the way a film title sits on a frame. The figure, with its unit, is at clamp(120px, 17vw, 280px), leading 0.8, in paper colour, hugging the bottom-left corner with 24px margins, its baseline nearly on the photograph's lower edge. A neutral dark scrim covers only the bottom 35% of the image for legibility. On the same baseline at the right margin, right-aligned, a sentence of up to 26ch at 18px explains the figure. At the top-left, small at 20–24px, sits the heading of two to four words; the middle of the photograph stays clear. Two smaller supporting figures may follow below the photograph, on the ground: each at 40px with a one-line caption beside it, starting at columns 1 and 7, 40px under the image. Choose a figure that belongs to the picture: a height, a distance, a temperature, a year.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 80svh, cropped to its subject. The figure sits bottom-left at 30vw; the sentence moves above it at 16px, left-aligned. Supporting figures stack under the photograph at 32px, each with its caption on the line beneath.

sections.name: One frame, three distances
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. On the stage one frame is centred: 30vw wide at 4:5, square corners, overflow hidden. Inside it the same photograph is shown at three distances as the reader scrolls: the whole subject, then scaled to 180% toward one detail, then to 320% on a second detail (transform: scale with a transform-origin per stage, 700ms ease, switched by IntersectionObserver on three invisible markers). The sentence is delivered in halves: its first two or three words sit above the frame at clamp(56px, 8vw, 130px), centred; the last words arrive below the frame at the second stage, overlapping the frame's bottom edge by 0.3em. At the third stage one caption of 28ch at 17px appears to the right of the frame, top-aligned. The two halves together are the heading and stay within two lines.
sections.mobile: The frame grows to 70vw at 4:5 and stays sticky at centre. The first half of the sentence sits above it at 13vw, the second half below it at the same size. The third-stage caption appears under the sentence at 16px, centred.

sections.name: Full panels, one midline row
sections.blueprint: Four to seven consecutive panels, each 100vw by 100svh, butted together with no gap. Each panel is one photograph of the project cropped much tighter than its frame (`object-fit: cover` with the image scaled to 130%), so a detail fills the screen. The same three-part text row sits at exactly 50% of the height on every panel, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` or over a neutral dark scrim band 90px tall: the date or year at the left margin at 15px, the project title in capitals at clamp(22px, 2vw, 30px) starting 10% in from the left, and one fact (location, client, number of pieces) at the right margin at 15px. Because the row never moves, scrolling reads like turning plates in a book. Panels may be `position: sticky; top: 0` so each slides over the last. There is no section heading; the first panel's title row is the heading.
sections.mobile: Panels are 100vw by 82svh. The row drops to the bottom of each panel, 20px above its edge: the title at 22px on the first line, then date at the left and fact at the right on a second line at 13px, over the same scrim band.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: Names running off the edges
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed band in a flat colour, about 34vh tall, holding a single line of names that is cropped by both viewport edges. The names are set at 8vw in the display weight, `white-space: nowrap`, separated by a solid round dot one third of the cap height, and the line moves slowly to the left (a CSS `translateX` animation over 40 seconds on a duplicated track, paused under `prefers-reduced-motion`). The band has no heading. Its meaning comes from one sentence at 18px set directly below the band at the left margin on the page ground, stating plainly who these names are. Supplied logos may replace names if all are available as single-colour SVGs at 0.8em height; do not mix logos and set names in one line. The band butts against the sections above and below with no gap.
sections.mobile: The band is 22vh tall with names at 15vw, still cropped at both edges and still moving. The explaining sentence sits under it at 16px with 20px margins. Do not add a second line running the opposite way; one line is the idea.

sections.name: Inset panel, shaped portrait
sections.blueprint: A deep-toned panel inset 20px from the page edges with a 12px radius, about 110svh tall, `overflow: hidden`. Left half: a two-line statement of four to seven words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 64px) in a pale ink, top-left with 56px padding; it is the heading and has nothing above it. Below it a photograph of the person or the workshop, masked with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask` to one bold shape taken from the subject (a four-lobed flower, a circle, an arch, a chamfered block), 38vw across, positioned so the panel's bottom edge crops its lowest fifth. Right side, starting at 63% of the width and 56px from the top: two text blocks 300px wide and 64px apart, each a subhead at 22px over a four-line paragraph at 15px; then one solid button in the accent colour. Between the statement and the text blocks the panel is empty. One photograph only.
sections.mobile: The panel is inset 10px and stacks: the statement at 8.5vw, then the two text blocks at full width, the button, and last the shaped photograph at 86vw across, centred and cropped by the panel's bottom edge by a quarter of its height.

sections.name: The object returns
sections.blueprint: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page. On one flat field 90svh tall, the object's photograph occupies columns 1–8, scaled to about 130% of that area and anchored so the section's bottom and left edges crop it (`overflow: hidden` on the section; on light fields `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes a white studio background). The text sits small in columns 10–12, vertically centred: a closing line of three to five words at 32–40px, one sentence at 17px, the price or key fact on its own line at 22px, and one rectangular button. Nothing overlaps the object's focal area. Where the page's subject is a shape rather than a photograph, the page's motif takes the object's place at the same scale as a flat filled shape. The closing line is the only heading.
sections.mobile: The text block comes first: closing line at 28px, sentence, fact, full-width button. The object follows at 130% of the screen width, shifted so the right and bottom edges crop it, filling about 55svh on the same flat field.

sections.name: Name across the last photograph
sections.blueprint: The footer is the page's last photograph, full-bleed at 100vw by 100svh, darkened evenly with `filter: brightness(0.62)` so paper-coloured type reads everywhere on it. Three layers of text sit on the image. Top row, 32px from the edge: a short link list at 16px at the left margin and contact details at the right margin, each no wider than three columns. Mid-height is left to the photograph. Along the bottom, the wordmark runs the full width in the paper colour, letters about 12–20vw tall depending on the name's length, baseline 56px above the edge; under it one line of legal text at 13px. Choose an image whose interest is in its middle band, since the top and bottom carry text. No panel, no box and no colour block separates the footer from the image: the photograph is the footer.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 88svh, cropped to its strongest vertical slice. Links stack at the top-left at 16px, contact beneath them. The wordmark is fitted to the width along the bottom, with the legal line under it at 12px.

references.name: The Watch
references.idea: A single 3D watch is the only actor: it holds centre stage and turns, flips and finally explodes into parts while giant product-name letters slide behind and in front of it.
references.hero: Light grey field with soft darker blurs toward the corners. A steel chronograph rendered in 3D stands upright at dead centre, about 80% of viewport height. Behind it the product name is set once across the full width in a wide, squared geometric sans at 24vw in mid-grey; the watch covers the middle character, so only two letters at the left edge and two at the right are readable. A thin circle about 700px across with faint radial spokes and one darker arc sits behind the watch like a dial diagram. No navigation, logo, body copy or button anywhere.
references.type: Nekst, a wide squared geometric sans, regular weight, uppercase, used only huge (up to 25vw) in black, mid-grey and white within one line stack. Body is Inter at 12px in 130px columns, roughly a 30x jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #e8e8e8 #c7c7c7 #a1a1a1 #6b6b6b #0a0a0a #ffffff — Entirely greyscale: pale grey ground with out-of-focus darker clouds, type in black, grey and white. The page darkens to mid-grey for the exploded view. Only the brass gear train adds warmth.
references.imagery: One real-time 3D steel watch shown front, three-quarter, caseback and exploded into dial, movement and plates lined up on a horizontal axis. No photographs; the object floats with no ground shadow.
references.layout: No grid chrome at all: the object holds the centre while type moves around it. Giant letters crop at any edge, captions sit in a 130px column left or right of the watch, and one product label is rotated 90 degrees.

sections.description: Four stacked lines of uppercase display type about 110px tall, flush left at mid-page and running off the right edge: line one mid-grey, line two black, lines three and four pale grey to white. The watch, tilted three-quarter, floats over the upper right of the stack and hides parts of letters, so type and object share the same space instead of sitting side by side.

The watch is turned to show its open caseback, placed just left of centre. To its right, a 130px-wide column holds two micro-paragraphs at 12px, each with a grey one-line title above. A small grey circular toggle sits far left. A white display word crops off the top edge. The rest of the frame is empty grey with a darker blurred cloud at upper right.

Exploded view. The ground shifts to a mid-grey vertical gradient with a faint horizon line. The watch's components (dial, tourbillon, movement, barrel, bridges) are separated and spaced along one horizontal axis at eye level like specimens. Tiny part names are set vertically along the bottom edge under each piece; a small prompt with a plus icon sits top-centre.

steal: Set the product name so large that the product itself replaces one of its characters, leaving the name half-hidden and the object as the missing letter.
Stack one display line in three tints (black, mid-grey, white) on a grey ground so a single typeface produces depth without colour.
End a product story with an exploded view laid out on one horizontal axis with vertical micro-labels instead of a spec table.
references.media: One fixed full-bleed WebGL canvas renders every picture: a steel chronograph about 620px tall (69% of the height, 29% of the width) centred inside a 720px ring with the giant model code behind it, then the watch from every side, an exploded line of parts on an axis with leader labels, particle ribbons on black, a black-finish reprise and a close-up cropped by the bottom edge. No photographs and no video; two very tall gradient overlays hand the ground from light to dark and back.
references.motion: The preloader holds at least 4.5s on the 3D assets, then its 720px circle stays to become the ring round the watch while a dark arc draws clockwise over 1.2s. Lenis drives one pinned, scrubbed timeline over 38 screens: the watch turns, separates into parts, the ground moves from #ebebeb to #a1a1a1 to #0a0a0a, and headline lines change colour by their distance from the viewport centre; per-character transforms are written every frame, smoothed by a 20ms ease-out.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: Transport
references.idea: Present a USB stick as a luxury object: one studio render on charcoal above a chrome custom wordmark, then let moody macro photography carry the rest.
references.hero: Flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a cut-out render of the drive about 31% of viewport width with its steel arm swung up at 30 degrees. Under it a chrome, ultra-wide custom wordmark spans 72% of the width on one line yet is only 45px tall. Then a centred serif tagline at 2.6vw and a single row: mono spec, a dark pill showing price and sold-out state, mono spec. Logo top-left, a grey centred nav prompt, a small pill with a glowing dot top-right. Carousel chevrons sit at the far left and right edges at product height. The bottom fifth is empty.
references.type: Three voices: a chrome extended techno wordmark as image; Untitled Serif 400 at 38px with -0.026em tracking for taglines and body; ISO mono for specs and caps eyebrows. Section heads switch to a tight heavy Untitled Sans near 36px. Nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #1c1c1c #c8c5ba #6e6f6a #5b5d45 #f1f1ef #2d2d2d — Charcoal base with white text; colour comes only from photographs in grey-olive, concrete and amber. One section flips to dark text over a pale blurred photo.
references.imagery: One clean product render, then shallow-focus macro photographs of the translucent drive on cutting mats, concrete and fabric, graded olive-grey with grain. Full-bleed bands with feathered edges, plus a row of rounded cards of unequal widths.
references.layout: Centred hero, then full-bleed photo bands each carrying one short text group placed differently: top-left, centre-right over a card, bottom-left, centred. Band edges dissolve through heavy blur instead of hard cuts. About 160 words across eleven screens.

sections.description: Full-bleed pale out-of-focus photograph with the drive in sharp focus in the lower half. Dark text overlays the top: a heavy tight grotesk heading at about 36px, left-aligned 8% in from the edge, then three equal columns, each a tiny glyph plus mono caps label over two lines of serif copy. No cards or dividers; the photo's soft blur is the only background.

A full-width macro photo band fades out through a blurred lower edge. On charcoal beneath it, one row of four rounded-corner image cards of unequal widths (one double-width, three single) with narrow gaps, each a tightly cropped lifestyle shot in a different colour temperature. The row is cut by the viewport bottom; further down one card grows taller and pins beside a short text group.

Dark band over a concrete-wall photograph. The drive render floats at top centre, half out of frame, with a horizontal motion streak smeared across the wall behind it. Text sits bottom-left: mono caps eyebrow, heavy grotesk heading, two lines of serif. The band cross-dissolves into an olive bokeh photo holding a centred mono equation, heading and one serif line whose quantities are joined by italic conjunctions.

Two small white script-lettered badges side by side at top centre, like garment labels, with a tiny pill link beneath, then a mostly empty charcoal field. Bottom-left, three tiny stacked mono link groups; bottom-right, white card-suit icons above a two-line italic mono credit, right-aligned.

steal: Pair one centred product cut-out with a very wide, very short metallic wordmark so the logo reads as an engraved nameplate.
Give three typefaces strict jobs: serif for sentences, mono for specs and eyebrows, heavy grotesk for section heads.
Blur the top and bottom edges of full-bleed photo bands so sections melt into each other with no hard seams.
